title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: 20% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift from 18 past 20% off promotions: x2.09; deeper discounts (30%) had higher lift (x3.1–3.3), so x2.09 is high for this level. Adjusted to x1.8 based on prior 20% off without seasonality.

drivers.name: Store closure (Mon)
drivers.evidence: One day closed; average daily sales ~96.6, so ~20% of weekly volume lost. No evidence of catch-up buying; no promotion before, so no pantry-loading. Reduction estimated at -15%.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion is similar to past 20% off events (x2.09 noise-adjusted), but the 30% off events were stronger (x3.1, x3.32). The 2026-08-24 week had both a 30% off and back-to-school season, which may have amplified lift. This week has only the promotion and no seasonal lift. Store closure on Monday reduces demand, likely by ~15% (one day lost, but 20% off may offset partially). The classical model’s x2.09 is too high—no prior 20% off had a 30% discount or seasonality. Adjust down to x1.8. Noise-adjusted effect is reliable due to 18 past promotions. No pantry-loading effect expected (first promotion this month).

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 8.26 (-16.4% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.9 - 233.3 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
